cost_metric: total model input plus output tokens

findings.title: A malformed GLM inspection call ends the run before the model can repair it

evidence.claim: validateCalls throws a typed GlmError for an invalid batch.
Validation occurs before any tool result is appended; the outer catch returns BLOCK. The typed host reason is retained, but no correction reaches the model.

findings.reproduction: Call validateCalls with a read-file call that omits path. It throws glm.tool-arguments-invalid; runGlmAgent catches it and terminates rather than appending a rejected-call observation.
findings.likely_token_impact: All tokens already spent on the episode become unable to contribute to a completed repair; a fresh episode would repeat context and investigation tokens.
findings.repair_candidate: Represent safe schema/protocol rejection as a bounded tool result, consume one turn, and continue when the remaining completion budget is sufficient. Keep batch validation before effects.
findings.meaningful_validation: An integration test emits one malformed read, receives field-level corrective feedback, then performs the valid read and submits a verified candidate; mixed batches still execute no calls until the whole batch is admitted.

findings.title: Recovery reservation can remove the read tool required by its own staging correction

evidence.claim: The reserved checkpoint exposes only record/report at step 10 and stage/report at step 14 while no candidate exists.
A failed exact match explicitly instructs the model to reread original source.
At step 14 the model used report_unable with reason placeholder; no read tool was available at the checkpoint.

findings.reproduction: At reserved step 14 with hypotheses present and candidates empty, phaseFor returns stage_patch_candidate and report_unable only. Make staging return old_text must match exactly once; the next phase still cannot expose read_file.
findings.likely_token_impact: Reserved turns cannot be spent on the evidence needed to correct a rejected edit, so prior investigation tokens do not lead to a candidate and the remaining calls collapse into repeated invalid staging or inability.
findings.repair_candidate: Make reservation outcome-driven: after a staging rejection, expose one source-bound recovery read or a typed exact-match helper while preserving the test/finalize reserve.
findings.meaningful_validation: A deterministic phase test drives an old_text mismatch at the checkpoint and proves the next turn can recover the exact source, restage once, test, and terminate within the fixed budget.

findings.title: GLM paging is applied after the read runtime's 65,536-byte result limit

evidence.claim: read-file serializes the whole file and rejects results above maximum_result_bytes.
The agent invokes full read-file first and only then calls pageObservation.
Paging expects an already successful full-file observation.

findings.reproduction: A local call to createReadOnlyToolRuntime with the 149,356-byte feedback-timing closeout.json allowlisted returned {ok:false, reason_codes:["tool.result-limit-exceeded"]}; the page adapter receives no source body to slice.
findings.likely_token_impact: The model may spend read turns retrying a file that the advertised paging contract cannot deliver, and a required-read completion gate can become unsatisfiable.
findings.repair_candidate: Implement range-aware reading below the result-size check and compute the full-file digest without placing the full source in the tool result.
findings.meaningful_validation: Read a source larger than the result ceiling in gap-free UTF-16 pages, verify every result remains bounded, assemble to the pinned hash, and pass required-file delivery without any full result.

findings.title: The advertised patch schema does not bind each path to its own file digest

evidence.claim: path and expected_file_sha256 are populated as independent enums.
parseSubmission later performs the missing path-to-digest binding check.

findings.reproduction: With allowlisted a.mjs/hash-A and b.mjs/hash-B, validatePatchShape accepts path a.mjs with hash-B against patchToolSchema, while parseSubmission rejects the same candidate as submission.scope-drift.
findings.likely_token_impact: The model can spend its terminal output tokens producing a candidate accepted by the shown tool schema but rejected by the local envelope parser.
findings.repair_candidate: Generate a oneOf/conditional branch per allowlisted path, or make one file-scoped submission tool per target, so the provider-visible schema expresses the actual binding.
findings.meaningful_validation: Validate every cross-product of two paths and two hashes: only the two correct pairs pass both the provider projection and parseSubmission.

findings.title: The native final turn offers submission even when required evidence is incomplete

evidence.claim: nativeReady is true on finalTurn regardless of gate status and replaces all tools with submit_patch_candidate.
The candidate is parsed, then the incomplete gate returns BLOCK.

findings.reproduction: Reach the final model request with completion_requirements missing one delivered read. The prompt exposes only submit_patch_candidate; a valid submission is rejected by glm.completion-requirements-unmet and prose is rejected as a candidate.
findings.likely_token_impact: The reserved final request cannot produce a successful or honest structured outcome, so its input and output tokens are predictably spent on a rejected terminal action.
findings.repair_candidate: Expose submit only when the gate passes. When it cannot pass, expose a sole structured report_incomplete terminal carrying the exact missing evidence, or terminate locally without another model call when the result is deterministic.
findings.meaningful_validation: Final-turn tests cover gate-passed submission and gate-failed incomplete termination; neither permits an unsupported patch and both yield a parseable terminal result.

findings.title: External staging repeats path in every edit and provides no source-bound correction

evidence.claim: Every edit independently requires path, old_text, and new_text.
Six consecutive stage calls omitted edits[0].path and received the same schema error.

findings.reproduction: Submit {edits:[{old_text:...,new_text:...}]} repeatedly; allErrors correctly reports the missing field, but the phase and contract do not bind the intended previously read file or change the correction strategy.
findings.likely_token_impact: The same schema mistake can consume several full model turns, including repeated prompt context, without gaining task evidence.
findings.repair_candidate: Offer a file-scoped staging contract after selection, with path supplied once and enum-bound to inspected mutable paths; add a repeated-error circuit breaker that changes the model-visible correction.
findings.meaningful_validation: A trace replay with the first path omitted must recover on the next call, and an identical second omission must terminate or switch to a stronger structured correction rather than repeating indefinitely.

findings.title: Repository read failures are collapsed into an unrepairable generic result

evidence.claim: All list/search/read execution failures become bounded repository tool failed.
A schema-valid read_file request failed with only that generic message.
The backend has distinguishable path, range, size, UTF-8, and operation failures before the runner erases them.

findings.reproduction: Request a schema-valid but untracked read path through the current runner. The backend distinguishes path not permitted; the tool result exposes only bounded repository tool failed.
findings.likely_token_impact: The model must guess whether to correct a path, range, encoding, size, or infrastructure condition and may repeat searches or reads.
findings.repair_candidate: Map backend failures to a small safe reason-code vocabulary with corrective fields such as requested_path and permitted recovery action; retain raw diagnostics only in local evidence.
findings.meaningful_validation: Tests independently provoke untracked path, out-of-range start, oversized file, invalid UTF-8, and infrastructure failure and assert distinct safe model-visible codes.

findings.title: Checkpointed task state is static while useful dynamic state is maintained by a separate runner

evidence.claim: boundState is cloned once and only re-presented; facts, lessons, completed, and pending are never updated by this runtime.
The runner initializes empty dynamic arrays and separately injects workflow.snapshot on every turn.
The separate workflow preserves hypotheses, candidates, tests, and probe counts, but not evolving source conclusions or decision rationale.

findings.reproduction: Record source findings without calling record_hypotheses, force recycling, and inspect meta.task_state: its facts/lessons remain the initial empty arrays. Raw history is archived, while the only deterministic dynamic presentation is workflow.snapshot.
findings.likely_token_impact: Recovering an archived byte sequence or replaying workflow metadata does not by itself restore the model's useful conclusion; the model may reread source and reconstruct reasoning with additional input and output tokens.
findings.repair_candidate: Keep deterministic memory maintenance separate from prompts, but add an append-only, source-referenced decision/fact state updated only by explicit typed tools. Render a compact projection of that state without claiming semantic understanding.
findings.meaningful_validation: A recycle test proves typed findings and unresolved discriminators survive, remain source-bound, and are rendered once; unrecorded hidden reasoning is neither claimed preserved nor synthesized by the runtime.

findings.title: Stable evidence is duplicated in every external-runner prompt

evidence.claim: The complete public context is inserted on every turn, then workflow.snapshot is appended.
workflow.snapshot repeats a sliced baseline excerpt already represented in public context.
Frozen prompts show public baseline/compiled evidence plus the repeated workflow baseline on later turns.
Captured current GLM prompts can contain an inspected-source projection and the retained original read result for the same source.

findings.reproduction: Inspect two consecutive capture.original values after baseline registration; unchanged public evidence is reserialized, and the baseline excerpt also appears in workflow state. In GLM capture, count the same source sentinel in source projection and retained tool output.
findings.likely_token_impact: Unchanged evidence consumes input tokens on every subsequent request and reduces room for source, tool feedback, synthesis, and completion within the same total-token objective.
findings.repair_candidate: Create one deterministic presentation planner that deduplicates content-addressed evidence across public context, workflow state, source projections, and retained tool bodies while preserving necessary stateless-request content.
findings.meaningful_validation: Snapshot prompt tests assert each content digest is rendered at most once per request, required evidence remains present after recycling, and repair outcomes remain independently verified.

findings.title: report_unable validates shape but not evidence quality

evidence.claim: Any non-empty reason and non-empty evidence-ref strings satisfy report_unable.
A valid-shaped report_unable is accepted as terminal without semantic or source-reference checks.
{reason:placeholder,evidence_refs:[a source path]} was accepted as unable_to_repair.

findings.reproduction: Call validateArgs(report_unable, {reason:'placeholder',evidence_refs:['x']}); then execute the current runner branch. It returns a successful terminal inability record.
findings.likely_token_impact: The terminal call can stop further useful work despite remaining evidence and turns; tokens spent on the run produce no actionable diagnosis for the next iteration.
findings.repair_candidate: Bind inability to typed obstacles and known evidence IDs, require remaining-budget/phase facts supplied by the harness, and keep free text supplemental rather than decisive.
findings.meaningful_validation: Reject placeholder/unknown refs, accept a source-bound obstacle with a current phase and exact failed tool/test receipt, and preserve honest inability when repair truly cannot proceed.

findings.title: Earlier staging exposed raw container stack traces, but the reusable path is now sanitized

evidence.claim: Old attempts returned the full command and container stack for an exact-match error.
The current revision path maps the error to a bounded message and recovery guidance.

findings.reproduction: Historical only: replay the frozen attempt-3 events. Current stagingFeedback no longer emits the stack for this known error.
findings.likely_token_impact: The historical response spent input tokens on irrelevant stack frames; this should not be counted as a current defect without a path that bypasses stagingFeedback.
findings.repair_candidate: Retain the current bounded mapping and extend it to the generic repository-tool path in TC-007.
findings.meaningful_validation: Regression tests assert raw command lines, temporary container names, and stack frames never enter model-visible tool results for every mapped staging error.

benchmark_families.glm-fitting-v1: Reviewed benchmark/live adapter and tests. This family deliberately exposes tools:[] and is relevant mainly to terminal response and token accounting, not coding-tool quality.
benchmark_families.glm-episodes-v1: Reviewed episode construction/runner, native submission probe, current GLM agent, tool schemas, delivery, paging, archive recovery, completion, submission, patch schema/runtime, read-only runtime, and selected captured evidence.
benchmark_families.external-context-v1: Reviewed shared contract/backend, current success/holdout/recovery-reservation contracts, phases, runners, workflow/recovery state, and programmatically inspected model-visible failures in every discovered evidence/*/events.json.
benchmark_families.real-reasoning-v1: Reviewed compaction/live surfaces and schemas. Tool-pair events are deterministic benchmark data or no-tools live prompts; this family does not provide the live repository editing contracts implicated here.

coverage.validator_assessment: The current external adapters call parseBoundedJSON plus closed Ajv schemas for every tool call, and the GLM native validator recursively checks required and additional fields. No missing whole-object validator bypass was found. The concrete gaps are semantic cross-field bindings, overly brittle shapes, post-schema backend errors, and controller behavior after rejection.

limitations: No provider calls, Docker runs, credentials, fixes, or new live experiments were used.
The companion trace audit owns exhaustive experiment-level aggregation; this audit sampled current captures and enumerated model-visible failures from discovered external-context events files.
Source-inferred defects are not labeled live-observed unless a frozen event or bounded local reproduction supports that label.
Token impacts are qualitative because the evidence does not isolate causal token counts for each contract defect.
open_questions: Should malformed read calls be recoverable inside an episode, and what minimum remaining-turn budget makes one correction safe?
Should the patch protocol remain complete-file replacement, add source-bound hunks, or support both under one transactional verifier?
Which dynamic facts deserve explicit deterministic capture, and which must remain model reasoning with no preservation claim?
Can prompt deduplication preserve stateless provider correctness while materially reducing total input tokens on the same fixed cohort?
Are all production consumers able to use conditional JSON Schema reliably, or is a file-scoped tool surface more portable?
